gaps.sentence: The new bridge, ___ cost two billion euros, opened last month.
gaps.hint: thing + extra information after a comma
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces non-defining clauses about things; 'that' is forbidden there.

gaps.sentence: Mrs Patterson, ___ taught me maths, has just retired.
gaps.hint: extra information after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: After a comma the relative clause is non-defining, so 'that' is impossible and 'who' refers to the person.

gaps.sentence: That's exactly ___ I needed — thank you!
gaps.explanation: 'What I needed' means 'the thing that I needed'; 'that' cannot be used in this free relative position.

gaps.sentence: Mount Everest, ___ was first climbed in 1953, attracts hundreds of climbers every year.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces extra information about the mountain; 'that' is wrong after a comma.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: This clock, ___ belonged to my grandmother, is still working perfectly.
gaps.hint: thing as subject; clause between commas
gaps.explanation: The clock is a thing, so 'which' is correct; 'that' cannot be used in a non-defining clause.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.
